## CVE-2026-118527: Ivanti Connect Secure Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers Vulnerability

Source-reported by [CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?search_api_fulltext=CVE-2026-118527).

CVE-2026-118527 (official CVSS 4.3): Use of predictable filenames in Ivanti Connect Secure before versions 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6 allows a remote authenticated attacker to upload files with attacker-controlled content to a known location on disk. CISA lists it as exploited in the wild.

Defensive action: Apply the vendor's security update; the CVE record lists the fix in 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6. If no update or mitigation is available, take the product out of service.

Limitations: Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue.

Added to the CISA KEV catalog 30 Oct 2026; first seen by SecOpsAI 30 Oct 2026, 20:51 UTC.

Identifiers and scores checked automatically against cve.org and NVD.

## LXD has argument injection in backup compression algorithm leading to AFW and ACE

Source-reported by [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fmc8-p6q7-75cc).

Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-v6mj-8pf4-hhw4 ### Summary Improper validation of user-provided backup compression algorithm leads to argument injection in the constructed command line.

Defensive action: Upgrade to a fixed release: github.com/canonical/lxd 0.0.0-20260630083100-c5184be310b1.

## LXD has arbitrary file write on client due to trusted image hash

Source-reported by [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pjff-c2wc-f6jm).

This can lead to arbitrary command execution as root on the server.

Defensive action: Upgrade to a fixed release: github.com/canonical/lxd 0.0.0-20260630083100-c5184be310b1.

Limitations: Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue. SecOpsAI recorded no CVE identifier for this advisory.

Published 6 Nov 2026, 19:36 UTC; first seen by SecOpsAI 7 Nov 2026, 21:10 UTC.

Checked automatically: primary source with a stated fix; no CVE to check.

SecOpsAI detection: no SecOpsAI rule covers this yet.

## LXD has restricted project bypass leading to arbitrary command execution

Source-reported by [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-47w9-6r3f-938g).

As snapshots can be moved from one server to another, a malicious instance+snapshot can be crafted locally, moved to a restricted project and the snapshot restored for arbitrary command execution.

Defensive action: Upgrade to a fixed release: github.com/canonical/lxd 0.0.0-20260630083100-c5184be310b1.

Limitations: Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue. SecOpsAI recorded no CVE identifier for this advisory.

Published 6 Nov 2026, 19:51 UTC; first seen by SecOpsAI 7 Nov 2026, 21:10 UTC.

Checked automatically: primary source with a stated fix; no CVE to check.

SecOpsAI detection: no SecOpsAI rule covers this yet.

## Banks: Unsafe importlib.import_module of attacker-controlled Tool.import_path in CompletionExtension allows RCE

Source-reported by [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-64vx-6h2c-rjh7).

CVE-2026-61536 (official CVSS 7.5): There is no allowlist or sanitization on import_path, so any importable Python attribute (e.g. os.system, subprocess.getoutput) can be selected.

Defensive action: Upgrade to a fixed release: banks 2.4.3.

Limitations: Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue.

Published 5 Nov 2026, 17:51 UTC; first seen by SecOpsAI 5 Nov 2026, 17:58 UTC.

## GitPython: arbitrary file read via attacker-controlled branch name in `Head.checkout()` (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-78679)

Source-reported by [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-23mf-xhv8-69c2).

GitPython: arbitrary file read via attacker-controlled branch name in `Head.checkout()` (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-78679).

Defensive action: Upgrade to a fixed release: GitPython 3.2.0.

Limitations: Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue. SecOpsAI recorded no CVE identifier for this advisory.

Published 27 Oct 2026, 15:28 UTC; first seen by SecOpsAI 27 Oct 2026, 16:20 UTC.

Checked automatically: primary source with a stated fix; no CVE to check.

SecOpsAI detection: no SecOpsAI rule covers this yet.

## dcmjs: DS/IS VALUE REPRESENTATION INPUT VALIDATION BYPASS

Source-reported by [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-px68-xx5g-48q5).

dcmjs, a JavaScript library for DICOM manipulation used in web-based medical imaging viewers, contains an input validation bypass in its handling of DS (Decimal String) and IS (Integer String) value representations.

Defensive action: Upgrade to a fixed release: dcmjs 0.52.0.

Limitations: Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue. SecOpsAI recorded no CVE identifier for this advisory.

Published 27 Oct 2026, 13:29 UTC; first seen by SecOpsAI 27 Oct 2026, 15:12 UTC.

Checked automatically: primary source with a stated fix; no CVE to check.

SecOpsAI detection: no SecOpsAI rule covers this yet.
